model: none - no image model was called and nothing was spent
graded_note: A6b, grade once - here, zero times. The source painting death-beholder.webp was itself ingested ungraded in phase AN4a (a colour boss: the grayscale grade would erase its orange corona and green hide), so these cells carry no grade either, and graded: false on the frame manifest says so. They match the static portrait they replace; grading only the animated cells would make the boss change colour the moment it starts to move.

source: art-department/masters/enemies/death-beholder.sheet.png (1408x528 lossless master, 8 columns x 3 rows of 176px cells; see its own provenance.json, which records the rig that drew it), itself rigged from the shipped death-beholder.webp (torio's `Death Beholder A.png`, 2022_added_monsters_ver3 pack, catalog slug `death-beholder`)
method: The rig keyed the painting's border-connected black ground to alpha and posed the whole sphere as one layer in 24 affine frames. The master was cut into 24 lossless PNG cells by the splitter, row-major, then each cell was encoded to WebP q44 by the shared ingest recipe with the grade skipped. Every pixel descends from the shipped painting; the sheet master itself never enters this tree.
used_by: components/combat/encounter/CombatCombatantPane.tsx - the Act 1 boss in live combat
measured: A8, measured on these exact files: 24 cells, 197658 B (193.0 KB) in total, mean 8236 B, max 11068 B (death-beholder-20.webp, the attack swell), min 4892 B (death-beholder-19.webp, the coil) - against 56286 B for the static death-beholder.webp. 3.5x, +141.4 KB for one enemy. The cell edge is 176px, not the float-eye's 256: at 256 this painting's cells encode to 21490 B max, past FRAME_CELL_MAX_BYTES (12000), and 192 still overshoots (12840 B). The ceiling held; the edge moved.
portrait_note: A7 (phase AN5a): the SHA-256 of the static portrait this set was drawn from. scripts/frame-set-portraits.test.mjs (root npm test) fails when the portrait's bytes no longer match: a swapped portrait retires this set (remove it or regenerate it from the new portrait).
